local_checks.invariant: No attacker-controlled key from the imported JSON reaches a recursive write or path assignment that modifies Object.prototype
local_checks.result: There is no deep merge or path assignment. The settings merges (storage.js:34, 237) are shallow object spreads (CreateDataProperty), so an own __proto__ key stays an own data property. sanitize copies only fixed DEFAULT_SETTINGS keys (storage.js:67-69). Game ids must match ^[a-z][a-zA-Z0-9-]{0,40}$ (storage.js:83), which rejects __proto__. Names such as constructor or toString are accepted only as own properties of the fresh clean.games object. Two assignments can use __proto__: MIGRATIONS[0] data.games[id]= (storage.js:38) and clean.options[id]= (storage.js:126). Each one only replaces the [[Prototype]] of a freshly created local object (data.games from defaultData, or clean.options). Neither reaches Object.prototype. The migrated games object is then re-read through Object.entries (own keys only), so the polluted entry is dropped. Object.fromEntries (storage.js:126) creates own properties.

local_checks.invariant: An object-local prototype replacement on data.options has no reachable security-relevant gadget
local_checks.result: With options.__proto__ set, clean.options inherits from an object whose values are strings under 40 characters. getOptions (storage.js:229-231) can then return an inherited string. In app.js:139 the spread of a string yields only index keys. createState in memoryGrid.js:48 whitelists variant to order or position. Option values are never rendered or used as attributes, URLs or code. JSON.stringify on save (storage.js:205) drops the non-own prototype, so nothing persists. There is no authorization, navigation, execution or rendering gadget, so validation rule 2 (prove a gadget) is not met.

local_checks.invariant: A request path cannot resolve to a file outside ROOT through dot segments, percent-encoded separators, backslashes, null bytes or a sibling-prefix directory
local_checks.result: ROOT is resolve(fileURLToPath(new URL('..', import.meta.url))) (serve.mjs:9), which is the brain-buddies directory without a trailing separator. The pathname is percent-decoded (serve.mjs:23) before resolve(ROOT, '.'+path) (serve.mjs:25), so encoded ../ and %5C are normalised before the check. The check file===ROOT || startsWith(ROOT+sep) (serve.mjs:27) rejects a sibling prefix such as brain-buddies-evil. Per documented Node behaviour, a NUL byte makes stat throw ERR_INVALID_ARG_VALUE, and malformed percent-encoding throws URIError. Both go to the catch block and return 404 (serve.mjs:36-40). Directories fail isFile and return 404. The only file operations are read-only stat and readFile, with no write, upload or archive handling.

local_checks.invariant: Symlink following and the stat/read TOCTOU gap cannot expose files outside ROOT
local_checks.result: stat and readFile follow symlinks, and the containment check is lexical. However, find shows no symlinks anywhere in the repository working tree, and the server cannot create files. Escaping would need a pre-existing symlink placed in ROOT by someone who already has write access to the developer's tree, which grants more authority than the read it would yield. The stat-to-readFile gap needs the same local write authority. Neither is reachable by a lower-trust principal.

local_checks.invariant: The dev server exposes no state-changing action and no protected resource to remote, cross-origin or rebinding callers beyond the static app it is meant to serve
local_checks.result: The server listens on 127.0.0.1 only (serve.mjs:43). Every method is handled as a read of a static file (serve.mjs:20-35), so there is no state change, upload, admin or debug endpoint, and requests carry no authority. There is no Host header check, so DNS rebinding by a web page could read files under ROOT. Those files are the game's own static source, docs and tests, which the server exists to hand to any browser. The rebound origin differs from http://127.0.0.1:<port>, so it cannot read the game's localStorage. Cross-origin reads are blocked by same-origin policy (no CORS headers are set). A local user reaching the port gets only files inside ROOT. No authority boundary with a protected resource is crossed.
